title: Why Arjuna and Bhima fell
hook: Arjuna falls, then Bhima, who asks with his last breath why he is falling
carry: prasad: food offered first, then shared
tomorrow: will heaven let Yudhishthira bring the dog?

segments.voice: Yesterday the twins fell, Sahadeva for his pride in wisdom, Nakula in beauty. Your line was amanitva: keep the gift, drop the ranking.

Arjuna, who threw his bow into the sea, is still walking. He's the one who heard the Gita in the chariot, who won Draupadi at her bridegroom-choice, who fought through the war. Then, on the high road, grief at his brothers' falling seems to catch up with him, and Arjuna falls too. Bhima, who has asked why each time, asks again. A little later Bhima the strong feels his own legs go, and lying on the ground, he calls out one more question, this time about himself.
screen: `ARJUNA STILL WALKING.` → `ARJUNA FALLS.` → `BHIMA ASKS ABOUT HIMSELF.`

segments.voice: About Arjuna, Yudhishthira's answer in Ganguli's telling has two parts. Arjuna once vowed to destroy all their enemies in a single day, and he didn't. And he looked down on every other bowman. Yesterday's ranking, in an archer's shape. Then Bhima falls, and this time he asks about no one else: I'm falling too. Why? Yudhishthira answers him directly. You ate too much, you boasted of your strength, and when you ate, you never thought of what others needed. Then he walks on. Bhima's fault is the most ordinary of all: a plate. And Hindu teaching has a great deal to say about a plate. The Gita, the teaching Arjuna heard in the chariot, says the good eat what remains after an offering, and those who cook only for themselves eat sin. That's why, in so many Hindu homes, the first portion goes to God before anyone eats, often a small plate set before the shrine. What comes back is prasad, food made holy by being offered, and prasad is always shared: with the family, the guest, the neighbor. Many families set aside a first roti for a cow or a hungry person too. A meal eaten that way is the opposite of Bhima's. Bhima, who asked why every time, is the last brother to fall. Behind Yudhishthira now, only one follower is left: the dog.
screen: `ARJUNA: A BOAST NOT KEPT` · `"YOU ATE WITHOUT A THOUGHT FOR OTHERS"` · `GITA: EAT WHAT REMAINS AFTER THE OFFERING` · `THE FIRST PORTION GOES TO GOD` · then, large: `PRASAD: OFFERED FIRST, THEN SHARED`

segments.voice: Before your next meal or snack, pause before the first bite. Many Hindus offer the food first, with a quiet line or a small plate set before God, and then eat it as prasad. If you pray, try it that way today. If you don't, name in your head three people whose work put this food in front of you, and share one bite of it with someone. Bhima's fall was eating as if no one else were at the table.
Bhima. The second Pandava, the strong one, who asks why each traveler falls, and falls last himself before Yudhishthira walks on with only the dog.
Prasad: food offered first, then shared. Hold on to that one. Tomorrow, a king, a dog and a chariot from heaven. Day eight hundred seventy-six, done.

screen: `DAY 876 COUNTS.` → `THE MAHABHARATA · 180 OF 182.` → `TOMORROW: WILL HEAVEN LET YUDHISHTHIRA BRING THE DOG?`

howItsDone: The falls of Arjuna and Bhima are told in the Mahaprasthanika Parva. The Gita's teaching about food is lived in many Hindu homes: a portion is offered to God before the meal and received back as prasad, which is shared, and some families set aside the first roti for a cow or for someone in need.
